analysis_refs.heading: 2. Scope
analysis_refs.text:
- Free to read: Project Gutenberg (local metadata import), Open Textbook
  Library and the bounded Book Dash catalog (owner-approved source expansion). Other free versions (LibriVox, Wikisource) appear only on detail
  pages as separate items, when a source links them.
- Papers: OpenAlex (when its key and budget are verified), Europe PMC, DOAJ,
  arXiv.
- Children's stories: the reviewed pilot set only, labelled as such.
- The library book page gains an "Also free to read" section.
- Desktop and mobile layouts, all three reading lights.

analysis_refs.heading: Query behavior and operating constraints
analysis_refs.text:
All six retrieval families—GDL, MediaWiki, LoC JSON, Internet Archive search,
LibriVox and Thoth—were probed with a nonsense term. Empty results were observed;
LibriVox expresses this as HTTP 404 with an audiobook-not-found JSON message.
An adapter must distinguish that documented response shape from an outage.
Representative second-page requests were also checked; retain each provider's
paging and scope. These checks are evidence, not implemented app behavior.

analysis_refs.heading: Query behavior and operating constraints
analysis_refs.text:
No paid fallback is proposed. All tested search requests worked anonymously.
Respect current provider limits and use bounded requests, cancellation, backoff
and truthful unavailable states. No numeric unlimited allowance is inferred where
documentation does not publish one. Wikimedia calls should be serial with a
descriptive User-Agent and maxlag for research; Internet Archive also requests
identification of automated clients. LibriVox documents a maximum page size of
500 and pacing for bulk work. We requested only three catalog records at a time,
except GDL's fixed 20-record search page.

analysis_refs.heading: Coverage and the next decision
analysis_refs.text:
If selected to advance later, prioritize GDL for children's coverage, Wikisource
for Indian-language literature, and the five Thoth publishers for shared
engineering. BHL and LoC add historical depth; LibriVox adds audio and requires an
appropriate listening-result design. Keep source qualification and new UI review
before implementation under the agreed workflow.

analysis_refs.text:

analysis_refs.heading: C05. Audiobooks and recorded books
analysis_refs.text:
**Best starting points.** [LibriVox API documentation](https://librivox.org/api/info)
describes ID, title, author and genre retrieval, JSON/XML responses and offset
paging. It presently caps `limit` at 500 and asks clients to space bulk requests;
recheck current policies before implementation. Use national-library audio
collections and independently maintained public-domain recording projects for
additional catalogs. [DAISY member organizations](https://daisy.org/about-us/membership/full-members/)
provide accessible-reading leads, with eligibility evaluated individually.

analysis_refs.heading: C05. Audiobooks and recorded books
analysis_refs.text:
**Search process.** Search `"{language}" "public domain audiobooks"`,
`"{institution}" ("talking books" OR audiobooks) (catalog OR API OR RSS)`,
and native-script equivalents for recorded stories/books. Follow a catalog's
producer credits to independently maintained origins. Expand by language/country
and producer type; distinguish library catalogs, volunteer recording projects and
publishers. A LibriVox narrator, recording version or mirror is not a new origin.
Expect a lower qualification rate and document scarcity if 100 independent,
freely accessible catalogs cannot be established.

analysis_refs.heading: Evidence boundaries and next handoff
analysis_refs.text:
Documentation opens succeeded for IBBY, Parag, Book Dash, Gutenberg, OTL, DOAB,
Project Madurai, LibriVox, DAISY and NLS during this planning review. The research
tool returned HTTP 402 for StoryWeaver's open-content page, 502 for NCERT's
textbook page and 403 for DPLA's API page. Sugamya redirected to its current domain
but exposed no readable content to the tool. These observations establish neither
payment requirements nor source-wide outages. No credentials, source accounts,
outreach, bulk harvests or live query qualification probes were performed.

analysis_refs.heading: What the original checks established
analysis_refs.text: Structured responses were obtained from Google Books (using the configured key), Open Library, Internet Archive, DOAJ, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, Europe PMC, CORE, Zenodo, HAL, Wikisource, Library of Congress, and LibriVox. Gutenberg RDF and DOAB record/harvesting responses also worked. OAPEN's OAI service identification worked; a record import was not exercised.
